Test Case Name: Initialize: Express middleware fetches supported kinds from facilitator on startup
Description: Verify that paymentMiddleware on an Express app calls the facilitator /supported endpoint during server initialization and caches the SupportedKind list.
Preconditions:
1. Developer role (server-side)
2. Express app is set up with @x402/express installed
3. A mock or real facilitator is running and reachable
4. Route config with at least one PaymentRequirements entry is prepared
Test Steps:
1. Import paymentMiddleware from @x402/express
2. Define routes config with accepts array (scheme: 'exact', network: 'eip155:8453')
3. Call app.use(paymentMiddleware(routes, server))
4. Start the Express server
5. Inspect server.supportedResponsesMap
Expected Results:
Server starts without error
x402ResourceServer.initialize() is called once
A GET to facilitator /supported is made
server.supportedResponsesMap is populated with the returned SupportedKind[]

Test Case Name: Payment Required: Express returns HTTP 402 with PAYMENT-REQUIRED header for unauthenticated request
Description: Verify that a GET request without a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header to a protected Express route returns HTTP 402 and a base64-encoded PaymentRequired in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header.
Preconditions:
1. Developer role (server-side)
2. Express app with paymentMiddleware configured on 'GET /data'
3. Facilitator initialized (supportedResponsesMap populated)
Test Steps:
1. Start the Express server with paymentMiddleware on GET /data
2. Send GET /data with no payment headers using fetch or axios
3. Read the response status code
4. Read the PAYMENT-REQUIRED response header
5. Base64-decode and JSON-parse the header value
Expected Results:
Response status is 402
PAYMENT-REQUIRED header is present
Decoded value is a valid PaymentRequired object with x402Version, resource.url, and accepts[] containing at least one entry
Remarks: Covers §4.1 steps 2–3 and §8.3 UI state table row 1

Test Case Name: Full Round-Trip: wrapFetchWithPayment completes payment and receives HTTP 200
Description: Verify the full x402 happy path: wrapped fetch receives 402, auto-creates payment payload, retries with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, and receives 200 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE header.
Preconditions:
1. Client developer role
2. @x402/fetch and @x402/evm installed
3. Express server with paymentMiddleware running locally
4. Client wallet funded with USDC on Base Sepolia testnet (or CashSchemeNetworkClient mock)
5. Facilitator running (real or CashFacilitatorClient)
Test Steps:
1. Construct x402Client with an EVM SchemeNetworkClient registered for 'eip155:84532'
2. Call wrapFetchWithPayment(fetch, x402Client) to get wrappedFetch
3. Call wrappedFetch('http://localhost:3000/data')
4. Capture all network interactions (initial 402 + retry 200)
Expected Results:
Initial request returns 402
PAYMENT-REQUIRED header is decoded to valid PaymentRequired
A second request is sent with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header containing base64 PaymentPayload
Second response status is 200
PAYMENT-RESPONSE header is present
Response body matches the protected resource
Remarks: Core happy-path covering §4.1 and §4.2 full round-trip
